subject.title: Create Claw agent and root install record

question: Should OpenClaw adopt RFC #27’s consented Claw installation lifecycle as an experimental core CLI and persisted SQLite contract, including landing this mutating add slice before or together with its recovery slices?
rationale: The patch can be technically correct while still creating a new core product lifecycle, CLI contract, and authoritative persisted-state model; repository policy and the protected `maintainer` label require explicit human sponsorship of that direction.

options.title: Land a cohesive lifecycle
options.body: Approve the RFC direction and land the base, this mutation slice, and status/remove recovery in an ordered main-bound stack with fresh-install and upgrade proof.

options.title: Keep add read-only
options.body: Accept the schema and planning work but defer user-state mutation until the full lifecycle and recovery contract is ready.

options.title: Pause the RFC stack
options.body: Keep the PRs open or close the stack if core-managed Claw installation is not a product priority.

recommendation.title: Land a cohesive lifecycle
recommendation.body: Approve the RFC direction and land the base, this mutation slice, and status/remove recovery in an ordered main-bound stack with fresh-install and upgrade proof.

likelyOwner.reason: They have the strongest demonstrated technical context on the mutation, provenance, and state-owner boundaries and are best positioned to frame the final product choice for the appropriate project owner.
